_comment: Serialised story for Section 1 (A1.1), one episode per unit. Recurring cast: Sarah (English teacher from England), Aziz (student), Kamola (Aziz's sister), Bobur (Aziz's friend), Mr Karimov (school director). Every episode uses only lexemes taught up to and including its unit.

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: It is morning.
body.chunk_note: day name taught as a name

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Good morning. I am Sarah.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Hello! My name is Aziz.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Nice to meet you, Aziz.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Are you a teacher?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, I am. And you?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I am a student.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Nice! Thank you, Aziz.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Goodbye, Sarah!

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Goodbye!

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah, where are you from?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I am from England. And you?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I am from Uzbekistan. I live in Tashkent.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Tashkent is a very nice city.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Yes! This is my friend. Her name is Kamola.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Hello! Sorry, I am not a student. I am a teacher too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Nice to meet you, Kamola. Do you speak English?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Yes, and I speak Russian and Uzbek.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Very good! What is your phone number?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is not my phone. It is his phone.

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Sarah is here. Aziz is here too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Aziz, what is this?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is a pencil. And these are books.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And these books?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Twelve books and four pens.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Is that your bag?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: No, it is not. It is her bag.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And this computer?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is my computer. This is my chair too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Thank you. Now, please spell your name.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: A - Z - I - Z.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah, this is my family.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A nice family! Who is this?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is my mother. She is forty-two.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And your father?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: He is here. He is fifty. This is my grandmother.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: How old is she?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She is seventy-nine. She is very nice.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Do you have brothers and sisters?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have one sister, Kamola, and two brothers.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And this baby?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is my cousin. He is one year old.

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Sarah has a new flat in Tashkent.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Is it a big flat?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, it is small. But it is very nice.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And the rooms?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: There are three rooms: a bedroom, a kitchen and a bathroom.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Is there a table in the kitchen?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, and there are four chairs. There is a fridge too.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And the bedroom?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: There is a bed near the window. My books are on the shelf.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Is there a garden?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, there is not. But there is a garden behind the house.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Aziz, what do you do every day?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I get up at six. I always have breakfast at home.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And then?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I go to school. I study English and Russian.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Do you work too?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Yes, I work in the evening. I usually finish at nine.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is very late!

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I go to bed late. And you, Sarah?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I get up early too. I never eat breakfast.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: You do not eat breakfast? Every day I eat at home.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I read my email in the morning.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Aziz, what does your mother do?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She is a doctor. She works in a hospital.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Is her job good?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Yes, she does. But she is always very busy.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And your father?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: He is a driver. He drives every day.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Where does he work?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: He works in the city. He knows every street.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Who works in the market?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: My uncle. He works there. He does not have a shop.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And Kamola? She teaches, and she helps students.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Excuse me, Aziz. What time is it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is a quarter past eight.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: My work is at nine o'clock on Monday.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And on Tuesday?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: On Tuesday it is at half past ten.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Do you work on Saturday?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, I do not. I do not work at the weekend.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: January and February are winter months here.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: In England, winter is not nice. Spring is very good.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: In May it is very nice here. And in England?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: In August! It is summer in England then.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sarah, do you like Uzbek music?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, I really like it. It is very beautiful.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: My brother loves music, but he hates football.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is not good! I like football, but football is not for me.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: What is your favourite film?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I do not know. I like American films because they are funny.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: For me, films are boring. I like books.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Me too! English books are difficult for me, but they are good.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Kamola has a party on Saturday. Sarah, do you want to come?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes! Thank you. That is great.

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: Sarah and Bobur are in a restaurant.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: I am very hungry. Are you hungry, Sarah?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes, I am. Can I have the menu, please?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The soup is very good here.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Can I have some soup and bread, please?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: And chicken with rice for me, please. And a lot of salad.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Is there any tea?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Yes, there is. Do you want sugar?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, thank you. I do not want sugar in my tea.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Two teas and one coffee, please.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: How much is it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is not a lot. Can we have the bill, please?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Sarah, can you play football?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, I cannot. But I can swim.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I can swim too, but I cannot swim fast.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Kamola can play tennis very well.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And I can sing! But I cannot dance.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Can you play the guitar, Aziz?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Not very well. My hands are not good.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Our team plays in the park on Sunday. Can you come?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes! Can Kamola come?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes. Could you come at ten?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Ten is fine. Goodbye!

body.speaker: narrator
body.text: It is Sunday. The weather is bad in Tashkent.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Hello, Aziz. What are you doing?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I am sitting at home. I am reading a book.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Where is Kamola?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She is in the kitchen. She is making lunch.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And Bobur? Is he playing football?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: No, he is not. The weather is bad today. It is cold and it is raining.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: I am wearing a coat and a hat!

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Are you walking to the park now?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: No, I am waiting for my friend. We are going to the shop.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Look! The sun is here. It is not raining now.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Yes! I am walking!
